text:
anne: Heads-up — canary runs for aegis28b (int8) are hitting intermittent OOMs and a weird growth in free-list / heap fragmentation. Seen on 3 different hosts across two zones. logs: ```Allocator: trying to allocate 204800000 bytes
CUDA OOM at /workspace/runtime/alloc.cc:142
Heap free list: 12MB -> 48MB -> 132MB after warmup
KV cache allocations unchanged
Batch size: 8, max_new_tokens: 512```
anne: Repro steps: send 6 concurrent chat requests with mixed history lengths, one request uses a long system prompt. Not deterministic but frequency ~1/30 requests.
raj: :eyes: that's higher frag growth than i'd expect for int8. did we enable slab-evict or compaction for this canary?
anne: Not yet — default allocator settings for aegis28b were left as runtime defaults. Compaction disabled.
liam: Could the culprit be the large default max_new_tokens=512 — big tails allocate large temp buffers per token loop. Maybe reduce default for canary to 128 and see.
sophia: Agreed. Also check batching policy: we still use max_batch_tokens=8192 for this model, which amplifies peak per-device allocations. Try lowering to 4096 and enable `prefer_prefetch=false` for the first wave.
raj: Quick mitigation suggestion: set model config overrides for canary: `{
  "max_new_tokens": 128,
  "max_batch_tokens": 4096,
  "alloc_compact_interval_s": 30,
  "kv_prune_threshold": 0.8
}`
liam: +1. Also add a soft cap on concurrent sessions for this canary: reduce `concurrency_limit` from 16 -> 8. That will lower peak.
anne: Running a tiny experiment now — applying overrides to the canary pool on `zone-b` and restarting the workers. Will attach telemetry in a bit.
infra-bot: Deploy started: canary-config-update to aegis28b-int8 on pool-aegis-canary-zone-b by anne at 2026-03-21T15:04:25Z
anne: After the change, ran 300 chats through the canary for 10 minutes. OOMs dropped to 0, heap free-list growth stayed under 24MB. Latency delta: +6% p95 on short requests.
sophia: Good signal. Need to confirm quality/regression impact for int8. Did we see any quality delta vs fp16 baseline on our eval set?
liam: I ran the eval-nlg suite before and after quant on a subset (200 prompts): bleu/rouge roughly same, but perplexity on long-context prompts increased ~4% which aligns with the +p95 latency.
raj: For rollout plan: (1) keep conservative defaults for aegis28b-int8 (max_new_tokens=128, max_batch_tokens=4096, concurrency=8) (2) schedule a background compaction every 30s until we prove stability (3) run 2k-eval sweep comparing int8->fp16 on long-context set and collect quality regression alerts
anne: I'll open a follow-up doc with the eval buckets and concrete numbers. For now, rolling these safe defaults to dedicated staging and tagging the model as `safety-capped` until sweep passes.
sophia: One more note — add an automatic downgrade/fallback policy in the routing rules: if frag growth > 50MB within 5m, route new requests to the fp16 variant. Should avoid user-visible errors.
liam: Can we also add a quick server-side guard to reject requests with `max_new_tokens > 256` for this model unless explicitly allowed by an operator key? Simple defensiveness while onboarding.
anne: Good idea. I'll push both routing fallback and guard change as a quick PR after the doc.
raj: :thumbsup: thanks team. Great triage, anne.
anne: Thanks — will ping when the 2k-eval sweep finishes and attach the perf/quality graphs.
